name: Apply for a water abstraction or impoundment licence
fact: Environment Agency guidance sets application types, water-availability evidence and impact-assessment expectations and notes applications may be refused.
gate: Water availability or submitting an application is not a licence grant or guaranteed abstraction volume.

name: Hydrogeological impact assessment for groundwater abstractions
fact: Environment Agency guidance sets hydrogeological impact-assessment expectations for groundwater abstraction proposals.
gate: A completed HIA is assessment evidence, not the abstraction licence decision.

name: RPS 368 temporary dewatering from excavations
fact: RPS 368 published 23 April 2026 describes circumstances in which the Environment Agency will not normally take enforcement action for specified temporary dewatering despite underlying legal controls.
gate: An RPS does not change the law or create a permanent abstraction/discharge right; all conditions must be satisfied.

name: Pre-application advice for water abstraction licensing
fact: Environment Agency pre-application advice can indicate likely constraints and evidence needs for abstraction/licensing proposals.
gate: Pre-application advice is not a licence and can be superseded by detailed assessment or later water-resource conditions.

name: National Framework for Water Resources 2025
fact: The national framework provides strategic water-resource planning and abstraction context for England.
gate: Strategic water-resource planning does not prove a specific parcel has an available or connectable water source.

name: Flood risk activities: environmental permits
fact: Environment Agency guidance identifies works on or near main rivers, flood defences and floodplains that may need an exemption, standard-rules permit or bespoke permit.
gate: Planning permission does not replace a flood-risk-activity permit, and permit eligibility does not grant planning permission.

name: Register a flood risk activity exemption
fact: The official service sets conditions and registration steps for qualifying exempt flood-risk activities.
gate: Registration is not a bespoke permit, landowner consent or planning approval and applies only while exemption conditions are met.

name: Coastal change management areas guidance collection
fact: Government coastal-change collection updated 8 May 2026 links planning, relocation and local-authority guidance for communities exposed to coastal change.
gate: Collection inclusion does not itself map a parcel into a CCMA or determine planning outcome.

name: Shoreline management plans
fact: Shoreline management plans set long-term policy intent for coastal management, with delivery dependent on funding, approvals and future review.
gate: An SMP policy is not a funded defence project or guarantee that the shoreline will be held.

name: Using shoreline management plans in local development planning
fact: Current guidance explains how SMP policy and the SMP Explorer inform planning and development lifetimes in areas of coastal change.
gate: SMP policy context does not replace current NCERM mapping, local CCMA boundaries or proposal-specific coastal assessment.

name: NPPF chapter 14 climate, flooding and coastal change
fact: NPPF policy requires development to avoid inappropriate flood/coastal-change risk, remain safe over its lifetime and use sequential approaches where relevant.
gate: Policy compliance is a planning judgement and cannot be inferred from one map layer.

name: Risk of Flooding from Surface Water - Speed - Climate Change 1
fact: Environment Agency data updated 6 July 2026 models surface-water flow speed under a climate-change scenario using national/local modelling.
gate: Modelled speed is probabilistic scenario evidence, not measured parcel flood velocity.

name: Risk of Flooding from Surface Water - Hazard
fact: Environment Agency data updated 6 July 2026 derives hazard ratings from modelled depth and speed across likelihood bands.
gate: Hazard rating is model output and not certainty that a particular event/property will experience that hazard.

name: Risk of Flooding from Surface Water - Flow Direction
fact: Environment Agency data updated 6 July 2026 maps modelled direction of maximum-speed surface-water flow for defined likelihood scenarios.
gate: Modelled flow direction is not a detailed site drainage survey or guaranteed event pathway.

name: Risk of Flooding from Surface Water - Model Origin
fact: Environment Agency data updated 6 July 2026 identifies whether each location uses national-scale or compatible local modelling.
gate: Model provenance helps interpret evidence quality but is not itself flood-risk severity.

name: Main rivers collection
fact: The national collection identifies statutory main-river data and explains Environment Agency permissive powers for designated main rivers.
gate: Main-river designation determines regulatory responsibility but does not prove a permit is required for every nearby proposal.

name: Reservoir Flood Extents Individual
fact: Environment Agency data updated 12 June 2026 models dry-day and wet-day credible worst-case reservoir-failure extents and explicitly gives no probability of failure.
gate: An extent is a consequence scenario, not the probability that reservoir flooding will occur.

name: Risk of Flooding from Surface Water - depth/extents
fact: Environment Agency data updated 6 July 2026 provides probabilistic surface-water extent/depth thresholds across annual-likelihood bands.
gate: Depth thresholds are modelled likelihood evidence and not observed finished-floor flood levels.

name: Statutory Main River Map
fact: Environment Agency mapping defines watercourses legally designated as main river and distinguishes other ordinary watercourses.
gate: Main-river line mapping does not provide channel topographic survey, ownership or all permit setback details.

name: Coastal erosion collection
fact: The national collection links the National Coastal Erosion Risk Map and explains medium/long-term, management and climate scenarios.
gate: Collection presence is discovery evidence; exact frontage/scenario and local planning evidence remain required.

name: National Coastal Erosion Risk Mapping 2024
fact: NCERM maps projected erosion risk to 2055 and 2105 under shoreline-management and no-future-intervention scenarios and climate allowances.
gate: Projected erosion zones are scenario ranges, not a guaranteed future cliff line or funded intervention.

name: Statutory Main River Map Variations
fact: Environment Agency data updated 6 July 2026 identifies proposed main-river map changes subject to a legal notification/decision process.
gate: A proposed variation must not be treated as an effective statutory main-river designation until the legal process completes.

name: Risk of Flooding from Surface Water Key Summary Information
fact: Environment Agency summary information updated 6 July 2026 aggregates people/property/land exposed to surface-water risk by administrative geographies.
gate: Aggregate counts cannot be assigned to an individual parcel or used as a property flood-risk result.

name: Flood Map for Planning - Flood Zones plus Climate Change
fact: Environment Agency data updated 6 July 2026 shows how the combined Flood Zone 2/3 extent could increase with climate change while ignoring benefits of existing defences.
gate: The climate-change extent is an assessment scenario and not a guaranteed future flood boundary.

name: Flood Map for Planning - Flood Zones
fact: Environment Agency data updated 6 July 2026 defines present-day Flood Zones 2 and 3 ignoring benefits of defences; Zone 1 is all land outside those extents.
gate: Flood Zone expresses annual-probability bands and not flood depth, defence performance or certainty.

name: Historic Flood Map
fact: Environment Agency Historic Flood Map updated 29 May 2026 shows qualifying recorded flood outlines and explicitly says absence does not mean the area has never flooded.
gate: Recorded history is incomplete evidence and cannot replace modelled/current/future flood assessment.
